html:
Why we Created Custom Foam Balloon Sculptures Instead of Traditional Balloon Clusters for Teddy Bear Centerpieces


In the event industry, teddy bear floating centerpieces are usually created the same way: a teddy bear attached to a clustered ball of balloons sitting on top of a stick.

It works. It’s cute. But I knew I wanted something more elevated.

I wanted the centerpiece to feel more realistic, more sculptural, and ultimately more luxurious. Instead of the teddy bear appearing attached to a “ball” of balloons, I wanted it to look like the bear was actually floating from individual balloons tied to strings — the way real balloons naturally move and float.


That small design difference completely transformed the look.

The final result felt softer, more intentional, more artistic, and honestly much more high-end than the traditional clustered balloon method often seen in event decor.

But getting there took far more experimentation than I expected.


The Vision Behind the Design


One thing I constantly think about in event design is how to make installations feel less manufactured and more immersive.

Traditional balloon clusters tend to look very rounded and uniform. For this design, I wanted dimension and realism.

The goal was:
• Individual sculpted balloons
• Organic movement
• A glossy, luxury finish
• A lightweight structure
• Something unique that guests had likely never seen before

I wanted people to stop and ask:
“Wait… are those actual balloons?”

That reaction alone made the entire process worth it.

The Materials We Used

For anyone curious about recreating something similar, here are the main materials we used throughout the process:

Main Materials
• 10-inch foam balls
• 8-inch foam balls
• Foam carving/heating tools
• Sandpaper (multiple grits)
• All-purpose compound
• Epoxy resin
• Water-based acrylic paint
• Wooden skewers
• Hot glue
• Flexible wire
• Ribbon
• Faux florals
• Fresh florals
• Teddy bears

I’ll also be linking the exact tools and materials used in my Amazon storefront for easier reference: https://amzn.to/3UUl00E

The Process: Turning Foam Into Luxury Balloon Sculptures

Step 1: Carving the Foam

We started with 10-inch and 8-inch foam balls.

Using heating and carving tools, we shaped the foam to mimic the soft curves and natural imperfections of real inflated balloons. After carving, everything was sanded down to smooth the surface.

This step was important because perfectly round foam balls still don’t quite resemble actual balloons. Slight shaping helped make them feel more organic and realistic.

Step 2: Applying All-Purpose Compound

Once the foam was shaped, we applied a layer of all-purpose compound over the surface almost like a paste or skim coat.


This helped:
• Fill imperfections
• Smooth the texture
• Create a more refined surface

After it dried, we sanded everything down again and repeated the process with a second layer.

At this point, the balloons looked much cleaner and more sculptural.


The Mistake We Made With Spray Paint

Originally, we tried spray painting directly over the all-purpose coating.

It did not go well.

The surface and spray paint were not adhering properly, and the finish was inconsistent. This ended up being one of the biggest learning moments in the process.

That’s when we realized we needed a more durable sealed surface before painting.

Why We Added an Epoxy Layer

Instead of continuing to fight with the paint adhesion, we decided to coat the foam sculptures with epoxy resin.

This completely changed the game.

The epoxy created:
• A harder outer shell
• A smoother finish
• Better durability
• A more professional base for painting


Once the epoxy cured, we lightly sanded the surface again to create enough texture for the paint to grip onto.

That sanding step was extremely important because paint struggles to adhere to fully glossy cured epoxy.

Switching to Water-Based Acrylic Paint

After sanding the epoxy, we switched from spray paint to a water-based acrylic paint.

This worked significantly better.

The acrylic adhered properly, gave us more control over the finish, and allowed the balloons to maintain a clean, polished appearance before the final sealing layer.

Another Mistake We Learned From: Paint Cure Time Matters

One of the biggest lessons during this process involved curing time.

After painting, I waited about eight hours before applying the final epoxy coat. The paint felt completely dry to the touch, so I assumed it was ready.

It wasn’t.

As soon as the epoxy hit the surface, it essentially reactivated parts of the paint and created a mess.

That moment taught me something important:
Dry and cured are not the same thing.

Even if paint feels dry externally, it still needs proper curing time internally before being sealed under epoxy.


After that experience, I allowed the paint to cure for a full 24 hours before recoating, and the results were dramatically better.

Honestly, that lesson alone probably saved future projects.

 

Assembling the Balloon Structure


Once the sculpted balloons were fully finished, we connected them together using:
• Wooden skewers
• Hot glue
• Flexible wire

The wire allowed us to shape the “strings” naturally so the balloons appeared to float more realistically instead of standing stiff and upright.

To soften the appearance, we wrapped the wire in ribbon to resemble balloon strings.

That detail made a huge difference visually.

Finishing the Centerpiece

The base of the centerpiece was created using a combination of faux and fresh florals for fullness and texture.

We then placed the teddy bear above the floral base and secured its hands using a hidden rubber band so it looked naturally attached to the balloon strings.

The final result felt whimsical, sculptural, and elevated all at once.

Why Custom Details Matter in Luxury Event Design

This project reminded me that luxury is often found in the details people don’t immediately notice consciously — but absolutely feel.

Most guests may not immediately realize why the centerpiece looked different from traditional teddy bear balloon arrangements.

But they felt the difference.

The realism, movement, finish, and dimension created something much more immersive and refined.

And honestly, that’s one of my favorite parts of event design:
taking a familiar concept and pushing it just far enough to make it unforgettable.

Final Thoughts

This project definitely involved trial and error, but that’s often where the best creative breakthroughs happen.

We learned:
• The importance of proper surface prep
• Why cure times matter
• How different materials react together
• How much realism can elevate a design

Most importantly, we created something unique that truly reflected the luxury feel we were aiming for.

And now I honestly want to experiment with even more sculptural foam concepts in future event installations.

title: More Than a Grand Opening: How We Turned a Nail Salon Into a Valentine's Day Love Letter
author: Christine Osakwe
description: You know the kind of call that feels ordinary until you realize it's about to take over your next six weeks. That was Sammy’s call. Sammy had just opened a nail salon. It sat in a prime location, foot traffic and all. So Sammy came to us with a bit of a challenge he had wrapped inside a deadline: launch a grand opening
html:
You know the kind of call that feels ordinary until you realize it's about to take over your next six weeks. That was Sammy’s call.

Sammy had just opened a nail salon. It sat in a prime location, foot traffic and all.

So Sammy came to us with a bit of a challenge he had wrapped inside a deadline: launch a grand opening in time for Valentine's Day, and don't just decorate the space. I want it to feel like a moment. Something people would want to film. Something they'd want to be seen in. A space that would live and breathe love-season energy for an entire month.

 

The Ask Behind the Ask

What made this project different from a typical install wasn't just the decor, it was everything wrapped around it. Sammy didn't just want a pretty room. He wanted a statement. We found ourselves doing far more than our usual planning-and-design lane: sitting in on conversations with his social media management team, helping shape the marketing push around the launch, even curating the merch bags every guest would walk away with. This wasn't decorating a room. This was building a brand for Sammy.

 

Reading the Walls Before Touching Them

Here's the part people don't think about when they see a beautifully draped ceiling or a wall dripping in florals: someone had to figure out, first, whether that wall could even hold it.

This wasn't a ballroom or an event space built for installs, it was a working salon, with real plumbing, real electrical, real structure that had never been designed with drapery in mind. So before a single flower went up, our creative director,Christine, made trip after trip to the salon; five, six visits in total, armed with a tape measure and a mental map. She was slowly building every wall, every beam, every inch of moulding in the building.

Which walls could take a drill. Which ones hid a pipe that would turn one wrong hole into a flood. Which trim was structural, and which was purely decorative pretty, but never meant to bear weight.

To get it right, we brought in a specialist: Alejandro, who lives and breathes wood and metal structures. He walked the space, called out exactly which walls were safe to anchor into, and flagged the moulding that looked sturdy but wasn't going to hold a single drape without peeling off the wall within days.





View this post on Instagram










A post shared by Houston Event Planning, Design & Decor (@cococabana.htx)

 

The Overnight Build

Once the plan was locked, the real transformation began, and it happened almost entirely in the dark.

The salon closed at 7pm and reopened at 9am, which meant our only window to build a Valentine's Day dream was overnight. For three nights straight, the team moved in after close and worked until the space was unrecognizable.

Two-by-one wood slats got drilled directly into the safe points in the wall: sturdy anchors strong enough to hold drapery, but never touching the fragile decorative moulding that would have collapsed under the weight within days. From those slats, the drapes were hung, transforming plain salon walls into something soft and romantic.

Around the pillars, it was a different technique altogether: command hooks holding up pool noodles, wrapped and dressed until they became the base structure for cascades of florals. Nothing permanent. Nothing that would damage a space that belonged to someone else's business, but everything strong enough to carry the weight of a full-blown transformation for the month ahead.

 

A Salon That Still Had to Be a Salon

The trickiest puzzle of all didn't happen overnight, it happened on launch day itself, in daylight, with real clients walking in the door.

This wasn't an empty venue rented out for a party. It was a functioning nail salon that still needed to serve actual customers, and Sammy wanted it that way. A grand-opening discount promo meant guests could come get their nails done and be part of the celebration. So the team had to solve a spatial puzzle in real time: how do you fit a bar, cocktail tables, a saxophonist, a photographer, a videographer, and a crowd of guests into a room that also needs to keep its pedicure and manicure stations running?

The answer was a careful trade-off. About five of the salon's service stations were moved to the back to free up the floor, replaced with four cocktail tables and two chairs, each  just enough room for people to mingle, sip, and watch the space glow, without losing the ability to offer the service that brought them there in the first place.

 

Opening Night

By the time doors opened, the room had a full cast behind it: a day-of coordinator keeping the flow moving, a photographer and videographer capturing every corner, a bartender pouring, and a saxophonist filling the space with live music. Guests got their nails done under string lights and drapery that hadn't existed seventy-two hours earlier. They took photos in front of floral-wrapped pillars built from pool noodles and command hooks. They walked out with curated merch bags. And most importantly, they posted about it.

 

What started as a request to "help boost social media presence" became something bigger: proof that a grand opening isn't just a party, it's an engineering problem, a design challenge, and a love letter to a brand, all built overnight, one carefully drilled wall slat at a time.

title: How to Plan the Perfect Memorable Baby Shower Decor
author: Christine Osakwe
description: There’s something incredibly tender about a baby shower. It’s more than a party, it’s a quiet, joyful pause to celebrate a growing family.
html:
There’s something incredibly tender about a baby shower. It’s more than a party, it’s a quiet, joyful pause to celebrate a growing family, a moment to gather the people who care, and a chance to say: We are here for you, and we’re excited for what’s coming.

Decor doesn’t need to be elaborate to make an impact. What matters is that it feels thoughtful, personal, and warm. Whether you’re planning a shower for a friend, a family member, or yourself, here are some gentle, creative ideas to help you create a space that feels just right.

 

How to Plan the Perfect Memorable Baby Shower

1. Choose a Theme That Reflects the Parents

A good theme doesn’t need to be flashy. It just needs to feel like it fits.

Is the parent-to-be drawn to nature? Soft florals, woodland creatures, or natural textures might feel right. Do they love clean design? A neutral, minimalist theme might speak to them. Are they playful and fun? Maybe it’s a storybook, rainbow, or nostalgic childhood favorite.

Let the theme grow from who they are. That’s what makes it memorable.

2. Select a Gentle, Cohesive Color Palette

Start with a few colors that feel soft and calming. Think pastels, muted tones, or warm neutrals. Avoid clashing or trying to include too much, simplicity brings peace to the space.

Even two or three well-chosen colors can create a setting that feels calm, cohesive, and beautiful. Use them in your flowers, linens, balloons, signage, and little details across the room.

3. Make a Statement with a Focal Point

Choose one area where you can lean in, a space that sets the tone for the whole room.

A backdrop behind the dessert table, a decorated spot for opening gifts, or a photo corner where guests can snap memories, this focal point doesn’t have to be over-the-top. It just needs care.

You can use fabric draping, a wooden frame, a floral arch, a simple sign with the baby’s name, or a balloon cloud in your color palette. This is where people will gather, where photos will be taken, and where your love for the moment will show.

4. Add Thoughtful Personalized Details

What makes a baby shower feel special isn’t the size of the decor, it’s the details that feel like them.

A name sign. A framed quote about parenthood. A keepsake guestbook where people write notes for the baby. A little corner dedicated to the grandparents or older siblings.

These touches don’t just decorate the space, they tell a story.

5. Layer Textures and Fabrics for Warmth

Decor doesn’t have to be complicated—but layering makes it feel intentional.

Drape soft linen or muslin across tables. Add a lace or gauze runner. Use velvet cushions or throws. Place florals next to candles, or balloons alongside dried elements. These pairings add depth without noise.

Let the room feel like a hug, soft, layered, and safe.

6. Create Interactive Decor Moments

Guests love to engage, especially when it feels personal.

Set up a small station where guests can write wishes for the baby or advice for the parents. Provide plain onesies or bibs with fabric markers. Create a time capsule or prediction card activity.

These aren’t just decorations, they’re memories in the making.

7. Use Candles or Soft Lighting

The right lighting changes everything.

If your shower is indoors or in the evening, add votive candles, tea lights, or string lights. Choose warm bulbs and avoid anything harsh. If it’s during the day, let natural light in, and soften it with light fabrics or curtains.

Candlelight adds quiet energy. It slows people down. It makes things feel a little more intimate.

8. Incorporate Florals and Greenery

Even a few stems can brighten the entire space.

You don’t need grand arrangements—small vases with baby’s breath, eucalyptus, or soft seasonal blooms can go a long way. Drape a garland over the main table. Add a bud vase to each guest table.

Fresh elements help the room feel alive and grounded.

9. Set the Table with Simple Elegance

Whether it’s a full meal or just cake and drinks, the table is a gathering point.

Keep it uncluttered. Use real plates and glasses if you can. Add a linen napkin, a place card, or a tiny flower stem. These tiny additions bring charm and care.

It’s less about impressing and more about honoring the people sitting there.

10. Tie It All Together with Signage and Stationery

Print a small welcome sign. Use consistent fonts and colors on place cards, food labels, or activity stations.

You don’t need to over-brand the event, but a few signs that guide and ground the space help everything feel pulled together.

It’s like the punctuation at the end of a sentence, it brings closure to the story.


At the heart of every baby shower is love. Not just for the baby, but for the people gathering to support the journey ahead.

Decor isn’t about filling a room, it’s about setting the tone. It’s about choosing peace over perfection and warmth over flash.

So don’t worry about whether it looks “Pinterest-worthy.” Ask instead: Does this feel like love? Does it feel like home? Does it feel like us?

title: 10 Budget-Friendly Ideas To Make Your Event Memorable
author: Christine Osakwe
description: Elegance isn’t about how much you spend, it’s about intention, atmosphere, and the small, meaningful details that stay with people long after the event ends.
html:
Creating a beautiful event shouldn’t come with financial stress. The truth is, elegance isn’t about how much you spend, it’s about intention, atmosphere, and the small, meaningful details that stay with people long after the event ends.

If you are planning a celebration and wondering how to make it look lovely without stretching your budget, you're not alone. 

The good news? With a little creativity and thoughtful planning, you can create something that feels both warm and refined. Here are ten ways to decorate with care and style, without overspending.

10 Ways To Decorate The Budget-Friendly Way

1. Set a Realistic Decor Budget

Before you dive into Pinterest boards and mood-boards, pause and take a clear-eyed look at your overall budget. Decide how much you can comfortably allocate toward decor.

Once you’ve got a number, list out the parts of the event that matter to you visually. Maybe it’s a stunning table setting, or maybe it’s a cozy ceremony space. 

Focus your resources there, and don’t feel pressure to over-decorate every corner.

2. Repurpose What You Already Have

Take a walk around your home. Look in your cabinets, your bookshelves, even your garden. Chances are, you already own pieces that could work beautifully at your event.

Vases, candles, picture frames, blankets, crates, baskets, these everyday items can be transformed into charming decor with just a little imagination. A collection of mismatched jars can become an eclectic floral display. 

There’s something special about using what you already love, it adds meaning, and it costs nothing.

3. Choose a Simple, Cohesive Theme

One of the easiest ways to make a space feel elegant is to keep things visually consistent. Choose a color palette or theme that feels true to your style, and stick with it.

It doesn’t have to be formal or overly “styled”, it just needs to flow. Neutral tones with touches of greenery? Romantic and soft? Rustic and warm? Once you land on a vibe, let that guide every decision.

Consistency brings calm to a space, and calm always feels a little luxurious.

4. Use Flowers Strategically

Yes, flowers can get expensive, but they don’t have to. The secret is being strategic.

Opt for local, in-season flowers (they’re more affordable and often fresher), and mix them with greenery to fill arrangements without overspending. 

You can also choose just one statement floral piece, like a beautiful bouquet or table runner, and let the rest of your decor stay minimal.

Even a few blooms in bud vases can make a table feel complete.

5. Embrace DIY Projects

If you enjoy working with your hands or have a few crafty friends, DIY can be both cost-saving and deeply personal.

Think hand-made signs, painted jars, custom photo displays, or a simple fabric backdrop. Not everything has to be perfect. In fact, the charm often lies in the imperfections.

Take your time, keep it simple, and remember: you don’t need to do it all.

6. Rent Instead of Buying

There’s no need to purchase items you’ll never use again. Renting can be a wonderful way to get beautiful pieces, like tablecloths, chairs, arches, or lighting without the full cost.

Even if you’re working with a tight budget, renting just a few key items (like a striking set of candle holders or charger plates) can elevate your whole look.

7. Use Candles and Lighting for Ambiance

There’s nothing quite like soft lighting to make a space feel warm and elegant.

Candles, real or LED add instant atmosphere. Cluster them down the center of a table, line a pathway, or place them in lanterns. Fairy lights or string lights can turn a simple backyard or hall into a magical space.

Lighting doesn’t shout, it glows. And that glow is often what people remember most.

8. Get Creative with Table Settings

You don’t need a full set of fine china to make a table feel beautiful. Mismatched plates can be charming. 

Cloth napkins (even handmade or repurposed from fabric) add texture. A sprig of rosemary, a hand-written name card, or a small favor placed on each setting can make it feel special.

9. Incorporate Fabric for a Luxe Look

Fabric is a powerful tool. Drape it over tables, hang it behind a focal area, or use it to soften a plain wall.

A single flowing runner or curtain can transform a space. Choose colors that work with your palette and let the fabric add movement and warmth.

10. Focus on Key Impact Areas

You don’t need to decorate every inch of your venue. Instead, choose a few key spots that people will naturally be drawn to: the entrance, the guest book table, the head table, and the cake or dessert area.

Put your effort and budget into making those areas shine. People will remember those moments, and the rest of the space will feel complete simply by association.


Elegance isn’t about extravagance. It’s about making people feel cared for and creating a space that feels intentional, calm, and beautiful.

By choosing where to focus, using what you already have, and adding just a few thoughtful touches, you can host an event that feels personal without spending more than you want to.

title: 10 Creative Ways To Personalize Your Event
author: Christine Osakwe
description: Designing an event with personal touches doesn’t mean overloading it with monograms or making everything about you. It’s creating an experience
html:
There is something powerful about walking into an event and feeling like you know the person behind it, even before you see them.

The flower arrangements aren’t just beautiful, they are your favorite blooms. The playlist isn’t generic background noise; it is a soundtrack of shared memories. The food? It tastes like home.

Designing an event with personal touches doesn’t mean overloading it with monograms or making everything about you.

It’s about creating an experience that reflects who you are, honestly, intentionally, and without pretense.

Here is how to weave in those meaningful details that make it unmistakably yours.

10 Tips to Incorporate Personal Touches Into Your Event

Start with Your Story

Before colors and centerpieces, pause and ask: What do I want people to feel?
Think about your story, what you love, what moves you, and the moments that matter most.

Maybe it's a trip that changed everything, a quote that grounds you, or a ritual that’s been passed down for generations.

Let these things shape the design from the start. Your story doesn't need to be flashy. 
It just needs to be yours.

Customize Invitations and Stationery

Your invitation is the first glimpse your guests get into the event, it sets the tone.
Instead of defaulting to a template, think about what represents you.

Maybe it’s hand-lettered calligraphy, maybe it’s minimalist and clean, or maybe it’s a photo of a quiet place you love. Include a short personal note, a poem, or even a favorite lyric.

It doesn’t have to be grand; it just needs to be thoughtful.

Use Personalized Signage and Decor

Signs are everywhere at events, from seating charts to welcome boards. Why not make them part of your story?

Display childhood photos, travel snapshots, or hand-drawn illustrations. Name tables after your favorite books or places.

These are small choices, but they pull people in and let them see something real.

Incorporate Favorite Colors, Textures, and Scents

Design isn’t just visual, it’s emotional.

Think about the colors that make you feel calm or joyful. Choose linens or materials that remind you of your home or culture.

Add candles or flowers that smell like summer evenings on your porch or your mom’s favorite perfume. 
These things don’t shout, they whisper. But people notice.

Curate a Thoughtful Playlist or Live Music

Music is deeply personal. It brings back moments, and it creates them.

Build a playlist that reflects your journey, songs that played during milestones, that remind you of friends, or that simply make you smile.

If you’re hiring live musicians, ask if they can learn a few songs that mean something to you. A single song at the right time can move people more than any centerpiece ever could.

Offer Personalized Favors or Keepsakes

Favors don’t need to be expensive or fancy, they just need to feel sincere.

Think about something small but meaningful: homemade jam with a family recipe or a pressed flower with a note. These tiny gifts can leave a lasting impression, especially when they come with a story.

Feature a Signature Drink or Menu Item

Food is memory and when it’s tied to your past, it becomes even more powerful.

Is there a dish your family makes every holiday? A cocktail you always order on vacation? A dessert that reminds you of your childhood kitchen? Add it to the menu. 
Share the story behind it.

People will feel connected to you through it and probably come back for seconds.

Design Interactive Guest Experiences

Give your guests a way to connect, not just with you, but with each other.

Leave out a guest book, but make it playful: ask them to leave you advice, or share a favorite memory. 

Create a photo wall filled with snapshots from your life, or a station where guests can write notes and hang them on a tree. These little interactions invite people in.

Highlight Cultural or Family Traditions

Traditions carry history, meaning, and identity. Including them in your event can feel grounding and beautiful.

Maybe it's a dance, a prayer, a way of greeting or toasting. Maybe it's the food, the clothing, or even the way you open the event.

Sharing these traditions isn’t just personal, it’s generous. It gives your guests a window into your world.

Work with Vendors Who “Get” You

When you find people who understand your vision, everything feels easier.

Work with planners, florists, and photographers who ask about you, not just your Pinterest board.

The right team like Coco Cabana will help you tell your story, not turn it into someone else’s idea of perfection.

Trust your instincts. If someone feels like they just get it, they probably do.


When guests walk into a space that feels like you, they feel more at ease. They connect. They remember it, not because everything went off without a hitch, but because it felt real.

If you’re ready to plan an event that feels like home, heart, and everything in between, let Coco Cabana help bring it to life, with intention, care, and a personal touch in every detail.

title: 10 Travel Planning Tips for Destination Weddings: What You Need to Know
author: Christine Osakwe
description: Planning travel is just as important as planning the ceremony. If your guests can’t get there easily, the celebration falls apart. Think fast and in advance.
html:
Planning travel is just as important as planning the ceremony. If your guests can’t get there easily, the celebration falls apart. 
You have to start early and think through the details.

Why Travel Planning Matters

Your guests are investing time and money. They are taking the time to celebrate with you and the best you can do is to make sure the process is easier for all of them. 

Smooth travel means fewer headaches for everyone and poor planning leads to missed flights, confusion, and stress. 

So you have to be very clear on what to do. 

10 Travel Planning Tips for Destination Wedding

Pick Your Destination Early


Make sure you research weather, costs, and legal marriage rules. What are the visa restrictions? Are they strict? How can you and your guests cope? 
Also, make sure to ask how most of your guests can afford to get there.

Send Save-the-Dates Early
If you know you have a destination wedding in mind then you have to inform your guests in advance. Not everyone has the luxury of taking flights all the time, they need to plan for them in advance.

Make sure you are aiming for 8–12 months in advance and include cities, dates, and nearby airports for your guests to find it easier.
If you can take the time to help your guests plan time off work and budget travel costs, they would be appreciative of this.

Hire a Local Wedding Planner
These planners know the vendors, venues, and shortcuts. They speak the language and understand the culture and they will help you avoid some simple but costly mistakes if not properly managed.

Reserve Group Travel and Lodging
One of the great ways to reduce costs for your guests is to book hotel blocks to lock in lower rates. 
Also, look out for hotels that offer a mix of price ranges for guests, and arranging shared airport transfers will not hurt!

Set Up a Wedding Website
Your wedding website should have travel tips, dress codes, and schedules for your guests to get information at ease.
Include links to book hotels and flights and answer all your guests’ common questions in one place.

Plan Optional Group Activities
Your guests are traveling for you, make them unwind and help them have fun. Plan your welcome dinners or day trips and help your guests build connections.
Don’t forget to keep them casual and optional (Some guests would love to not be forced into activities they cannot afford). 

Pack for the Location


Think of the weather, terrain, and customs, and remind your guests to pack essentials: sunscreen, adapters, and meds. 
Also advise them to pack wedding outfits in carry-on bags, not checked bags.

Prepare for Delays and Logistics
Delays are natural and you can only do your best to avoid them so make sure to pad your schedule because flights can be delayed.
If you can get your dress/suit early, do that and make sure your documents are kept handy.

Know the Legal Rules
Some countries have residency requirements, check those out to prevent issues for your guests. 
You may need translated documents or blood tests so get those in advance and make sure you check the timeline for getting a valid marriage license. 

Use a Travel Coordinator
A dedicated agent (If you afford to spare the payment) or a friend can manage flights, rooms, and changes for you.
Your guests will get support without calling you and you will be able to stay focused on the wedding, not logistics.

title: A Coco Cabana Recap of Planning a Stunning Event
author: Christine Osakwe
description: Planning an event at Coco Cabana involves countless decisions. We recently brought a client’s event to life and we couldn’t have been happier with the result.
html:
Planning an event at Coco Cabana involves countless decisions, from design choices to budget management. 

We recently brought a client’s event to life and we couldn’t have been happier with the result.

So we have decided to create this post as a guide to help you create your planning process.

Planning a Stunning Event

Define the Vision

The client wanted a “dark tropical” or “moody tropical” aesthetic with a color scheme of reds, burnt oranges, pinks, and greens. 

So we made sure we prioritized minimal florals, dramatic drapery, and mood lighting to create an intimate atmosphere. 

Finalize Design Elements

20ft opaque ivory drapery was chosen for the ceremony to complement the client’s white dress and create a dramatic effect.

Bud vases and candles were arranged linearly on caterpillar-style reception tables for a minimalist look. Ceremony florals were repurposed for the bar, sweetheart table, and lounge areas.

Mood lighting with candles and tabletop lamps was used to enhance the ambiance.

Make Budget-Conscious Decisions

Red linen was chosen for cocktail tables, and one cocktail table was repurposed for the ceremony.

High cocktail chairs were confirmed with the venue to avoid unnecessary rental expenses.

Coordinate with Vendors

Vendors were booked only after finalizing the invoice and receiving payment to stay within budget.

Details like greenery for overhead décor, sweetheart chairs, and couch rentals were confirmed to ensure everything was prepared for the event.

Finalize Seating and Layout

A mix of comfortable couches and traditional chairs was chosen for seating.

The entrance table was designed as a multifunctional space for escort cards, guest books, and other items.

Floor plans were reviewed to finalize the layout, including drapery placement and seating arrangements.

Involve the Client

The client took charge of ordering and inputting names for escort cards to ensure accuracy.

Updated budget breakdowns were shared, and feedback was incorporated to align with the client’s priorities.

Prepare for Execution

Visuals in the Lookbook were updated to reflect final design choices, including reception table layouts and centerpiece arrangements.

Pictures of ivory drapes were shared with the client to confirm the material and color.

When next you have a client, make sure to not forget to:

  • Start with a clear vision and prioritize elements that align with your aesthetic and budget.
  • Repurpose decor items, like ceremony florals, to maximize your budget without compromising on style.
  • Involve the client in key decisions, such as escort cards and budget adjustments, to ensure their vision is realized.

title: Eru Iyawo: A Timeless Yoruba Wedding Tradition
author: Christine Osakwe
description: In Yoruba culture, the journey to “I do” isn’t complete without the Eru Iyawo, a heartfelt custom that bridges families through respect and gratitude.
html:
In Yoruba culture, the journey to “I do” isn’t complete without the Eru Iyawo, a heartfelt custom that bridges families through respect and gratitude.

If you’ve ever wondered about this cherished tradition, here’s a guide to its significance and why it remains a highlight of Yoruba weddings.

What is Eru Iyawo?

The Eru Iyawo, also known as the Bride’s or Engagement List, is a key part of Yoruba traditional weddings. It’s a collection of gifts and items that the groom’s family must provide to the bride’s family. This tradition symbolizes honor, appreciation, and the merging of two families into one.

Who Creates the List?

The responsibility of crafting the Eru Iyawo list falls on the bride’s family, typically led by the eldest family member. This elder compiles the list, which is then handed to the groom’s family well before the wedding. This gives them ample time to prepare for the big day.

What’s Included in the Eru Iyawo?

The items on the list reflect the values, customs, and beliefs of the Yoruba people. While specifics can vary depending on the community, some common elements include:

  • Money: A symbolic amount as a gesture of respect (often returned during the ceremony).
  • Traditional Gifts: Items like kola nuts, spices, and yam, representing wealth, health, and prosperity.
  • Personal Essentials: Clothing, jewelry, and accessories for the bride.
  • Faith-Based Items: A Bible for Christian families or prayer materials for Muslim families.
  • Celebratory Additions: Fresh fruits, sugar, and other delicacies to signify sweetness and abundance in the marriage.

Beyond the items themselves, their packaging and presentation have become significant, with modern families adding a touch of elegance and creativity to showcase their love and pride.

Why Does Eru Iyawo Matter?

This tradition serves as a heartfelt acknowledgment of the bride’s upbringing and the role her family played in preparing her for marriage. It also fosters a deeper connection between the two families, setting the tone for mutual respect and collaboration.

A Blend of Heritage and Modern Flair

As traditions evolve, so does the Eru Iyawo. While its roots are deeply cultural, modern couples and families often infuse contemporary touches into the process, ensuring the practice remains both meaningful and visually stunning.

Planning your wedding is one of the most exciting times of your life, but it can also be filled with challenges. 

Avoiding common wedding planning mistakes can make the process smoother and ensure your big day goes off without a hitch. 

That is why we have compiled the pitfalls to watch out for and tips on how to steer clear of them.

Wedding Planning Mistakes to Avoid 

Not Setting a Realistic Budget

A clear and realistic budget is the foundation of successful wedding planning.

Without one, expenses can spiral out of control. Start by:

  • Determining how much you can afford to spend.
  • Allocating funds to key categories like venue, catering, and attire.
  • Leaving a buffer for unexpected expenses.

Forgetting to Create a Timeline

A well-structured timeline keeps everything on track and ensures no detail is overlooked. 

Begin by:

  • Setting deadlines for booking vendors, sending invitations, and completing other key tasks.
  • Creating a detailed schedule for the wedding day itself, including setup, ceremony, and reception activities.
  • Share the timeline with your vendors and wedding party to keep everyone aligned.

Not Hiring a Professional Planner

While DIY planning can save money, it often leads to unnecessary stress. A professional wedding planner like Coco Cabana can:

  • Provide expert guidance on logistics.
  • Coordinate with vendors and manage the day-of timeline.
  • Troubleshoot issues so you can focus on enjoying your big day.

Waiting Too Long to Book Vendors

Popular venues, photographers, and caterers often book up months, or even years in advance. 

Avoid disappointment by:

  • Researching and booking high-priority vendors early.
  • Asking for recommendations and reading reviews to find reliable professionals. Coco Cabana is excellent at this and would provide high-level recommendations.

Ignoring Guest Experience

Your wedding is a celebration of your love, but it’s also an event for your guests. 

  • Provide clear directions and accommodations for out-of-town attendees.
  • Offer thoughtful touches like welcome bags or a curated playlist.
  • Ensure the timeline flows smoothly, so guests aren’t left waiting.

Overcomplicating the Decor

While it’s tempting to go all out with elaborate decor, simplicity often makes a stronger impact. 

  • Choosing a cohesive theme or color palette. You can also create your unique ones here.
  • Focusing on a few standout elements, like centerpieces or lighting.
  • Avoiding cluttered or overly busy designs.

Stressing About Small Details

It’s easy to get caught up in minor details, but they rarely affect the overall success of your wedding.

  • Focus on the big picture and the joy of marrying your partner.
  • Remember that guests will appreciate the effort, not notice every tiny detail.

title: How to Manage Wedding Planning Stress and Stay Organised
author: Christine Osakwe
description: Wedding planning can feel overwhelming, but it doesn’t have to be. With the right strategies, you can reduce stress and enjoy the process your dream day.
html:
Most people would get crushed under the weight of wedding planning but it doesn't have to be that way.

Knowing what to do and how to do them will help you reduce that stress and help you enjoy the curation of your dream day.

Which is why it is important to know what will be stressful and how you can avoid the anxiety that comes with them.

Why Wedding Planning Often Becomes Stressful

Planning a wedding involves juggling multiple tasks, decisions, and deadlines. From choosing the perfect venue to finalising the guest list, it’s easy to feel pulled in different directions. 

Add in family expectations, budget considerations, and unexpected changes, and the stress can quickly mount. 

But by staying organised and following these tips, you can keep stress at bay and focus on what truly matters.

Break Down Tasks into Manageable Steps

The key to effective wedding planning is breaking down big tasks into smaller, actionable steps. Create a checklist for each stage of the planning process. For instance:

  1. Start with broad categories like venue, catering, and attire.
  2. Break these into smaller tasks, such as visiting venues or scheduling dress fittings.
  3. Set realistic deadlines for each task to keep yourself on schedule.

Task lists not only make planning more manageable but also give you a sense of accomplishment as you tick off completed items.

Prioritise What Matters Most

It’s easy to get caught up in the details, but not everything deserves equal attention. Identify your top priorities early on; it can be the venue, photography, or a live band then allocate your time and budget accordingly. By focusing on what matters most, you’ll simplify decision-making and avoid unnecessary stress.

Delegate Responsibilities

You don’t have to do everything yourself. Enlist the help of friends, family, and your partner to share the workload. 

Assign tasks based on strengths. For example, a detail-oriented friend might excel at managing RSVPs, while a creative relative could help with décor ideas.

Use Wedding Planning Apps and Tools

Technology can be a lifesaver when it comes to wedding planning. Apps like Zola, WeddingWire, and The Knot offer tools to track budgets, manage guest lists, and even create seating charts. 

Digital planners keep everything organized in one place, making it easier to stay on top of tasks and deadlines.

Take Time to Relax

Amid the hustle and bustle of wedding planning, don’t forget to take care of yourself. Schedule regular breaks to relax and recharge. 

It can be a yoga class, a weekend getaway, or simply an evening with a good book, self-care is essential to maintaining your well-being.

Lean on Your Wedding Planner

If your budget allows, hiring a wedding planner can be a game-changer. Planners like Coco Cabana are experts at coordinating logistics, managing vendors, and troubleshooting last-minute issues. 

Our experience and connections can save you time and reduce stress, allowing you to focus on enjoying the process.

Stay Flexible with Changes

Even with meticulous planning, unexpected changes are bound to happen. Staying flexible will help you adapt without losing your cool. Keep an open mind, have backup plans, and remember that at the end of the day, it’s the celebration of your love that truly matters.

title: The Ultimate Checklist for Stress-Free Event Planning in 2024
author: Christine Osakwe
description: Here is The Ultimate Checklist for Stress-Free Event Planning in 2024: Set Clear Goals & a Realistic Budget, Choose the Right Date and Venue, Build Your Event Team, Create a Detailed Timeline, Develop a Theme and Concept, Plan the Logistics Carefully, Promote Your Event, Final Preparations
html:
Imagine hosting an event where everything goes smoothly. You’re calm, your guests are happy, and you can actually enjoy the day. Sounds perfect, right? With the right plan, it’s totally possible! At Cococabana, we believe a good checklist is the key to stress-free event planning. Here’s how to make your next event easy in 2024.


I. The Pre-Planning Stage: Building a Strong Foundation 

Before jumping into the details, it's important to have a solid plan to ensure your event goes smoothly.


Set Clear Goals & a Realistic Budget: 

Checklist: 

  • Decide on the main purpose of your event. 
  • Know your target audience. 
  • Set specific goals for what you want to achieve. 
  • Make a detailed budget that covers all costs. 
  • Research average costs for similar events. 
  • Set aside some extra money for unexpected expenses. 

Why It Matters: Knowing why you're hosting the event and who it's for will help guide your decisions. A good budget helps keep spending under control. 


Choose the Right Date and Venue: 

Checklist: 

  • Consider the best time for your audience. 
  • Avoid scheduling on major holidays or conflicting events. 
  • Find venues that fit the size and style of your event. 
  • Visit venues in person to make sure they’re suitable. 
  • Compare venue prices, features, and availability. 

Why It Matters: Picking the right date and venue helps set the mood for your event and ensures guests can attend.

 

Build Your Event Team: 

Checklist: 

  • List all the roles needed for the event. 
  • Decide which tasks you can do and which need outside help. 
  • Get quotes from vendors like caterers or photographers. 
  • Check references and reviews before hiring anyone. 
  • Clearly communicate everyone’s roles and responsibilities. 

Why It Matters: A reliable team is key to running a smooth event. With the right people in place, everything from setup to cleanup will go well. 



II. The Planning Stage: Making Your Ideas Happen 

With the basics in place, it’s time to bring your ideas to life. Good organization is essential here. 


Create a Detailed Timeline: 

Checklist: 

  • Break down the event planning into smaller tasks. 
  • Set realistic deadlines for each task. 
  • Use a calendar or project tool to track everything. 
  • Regularly review your timeline and adjust if needed. 

Why It Matters: A timeline helps you stay on track and avoid last-minute rushing. It also helps you catch any problems early. 


Develop a Theme and Concept: 

Checklist: 

  • Brainstorm theme ideas that suit your event and audience. 
  • Think about the vibe you want to create. 
  • Choose colors and decorations that fit your theme. 
  • Make sure the theme shows up in every part of the event (invitations, food, etc.). 

Why It Matters: A strong theme makes your event more memorable and ties everything together. 


Plan the Logistics Carefully:

Checklist: 

  • Choose a catering service that fits your budget and food preferences. 
  • Arrange transportation for guests if needed. 
  • Book accommodations for out-of-town guests or speakers. 
  • Get any permits or licenses needed for your event. 
  • Create a clear floor plan for the venue. 

Why It Matters: Proper logistics ensure everything runs smoothly, making your guests comfortable and happy. 


Promote Your Event: 

Checklist: 

  • Know your audience and the best ways to reach them. 
  • Design attractive promotional materials (flyers, social media posts, etc.). ● Use social media to build excitement. 
  • Consider paid ads or email campaigns to reach more people. 
  • Track your marketing efforts to see what’s working. 

Why It Matters: Good promotion ensures people know about your event and are excited to attend. It helps build excitement and attracts the right crowd. 


III. The Execution Stage: Showtime! 

Now that everything is planned, it’s time to bring your event to life. This is where your hard work pays off, but you still need to stay focused and handle any surprises. 


Final Preparations: 

Checklist: 

  • Walk through the venue to make sure everything is set up correctly. 
  • Confirm details with vendors, like their arrival times and setup needs. 
  • Double-check guest numbers and any special requests. 
  • Get any signs, programs, or handouts ready. 
  • Pack an emergency kit with useful items (like tape, scissors, and a first-aid kit). 

Why It Matters: Final preparations ensure everything is in place and smooth before your guests arrive, reducing any last-minute problems. 


Day-of Coordination:

Checklist: 

  • Assign someone (or a team) to oversee the event. 
  • Create a detailed schedule of activities and timings. 
  • Make sure all staff and vendors know their tasks and timing. 
  • Be available to handle any questions or concerns. 
  • Keep open communication with your team throughout the event. 

Why It Matters: Good coordination keeps the event on track and lets you focus on the big picture while your team handles the details. 


Handle Unexpected Challenges: 

Checklist: 

  • Have backup plans for common problems (like bad weather or tech issues). ● Keep alternative options ready for critical things like food or entertainment. ● Stay calm and adjust quickly to unexpected changes. 
  • Inform guests of any changes or delays in a clear and professional way. 

Why It Matters: Even with great planning, problems can happen. Being prepared and flexible ensures you can handle challenges without disrupting the event. 


IV. The Post-Event Stage: Reflect and Improve 

Once the event is over, take some time to reflect on how things went and gather useful feedback for future events. 


Get Feedback: 

Checklist: 

  • Send surveys or forms to guests and vendors to hear their thoughts. 
  • Ask specific questions about their experience and suggestions for improvement. ● Review the feedback to find out what worked well and where you can improve. 

Why It Matters: Feedback helps you learn what was successful and what needs tweaking, making your future events even better. 


Say Thank You: 

Checklist:

  • Send personalized thank-you notes or emails to your team, vendors, and guests. ● Highlight their contributions and express your gratitude. 
  • Share event highlights or photos to keep the positive vibe going. 

Why It Matters: Thanking people leaves a lasting positive impression and helps build strong relationships for future collaborations.

Conclusion: Stress-Free Event Planning Made Easy 

Planning an event doesn’t have to be stressful. By using a detailed checklist, you can stay organized and create an unforgettable experience for everyone involved. At Cococabana, we’re here to help you succeed. From planning to execution, our team of experts is ready to support you.

title: 10 Essential Event Planning Tips for a Celebration You'll Never Forget
author: Christine Osakwe
description: Ever feel nervous just thinking about planning an event? You’re not alone! That’
html:
Ever feel nervous just thinking about planning an event? You’re not alone! Whether it’s a birthday, wedding, or important corporate event, all the details can quickly become overwhelming. 

But here’s the good news: with a bit of planning, you can turn that stress into excitement and create an unforgettable event. That’s where we come in. At Cococabana, we believe event planning should be fun, not stressful. In this guide, we’re sharing 10 simple tips to help you plan like a pro. From setting the right mood to managing unexpected hiccups, we’ve got you covered. 

Ready to bring your event dreams to life? Let’s get started! 


10 Event Planning Tips to Ensure a Flawless Celebration 

  1. Define Your Vision 
  2. Nail Down the Budget 
  3. Choose the Perfect Date & Venue 
  4. Create a Guest List 
  5. Plan the Menu 
  6. Get Creative with Decor 
  7. Entertainment: Keep Them Engaged 
  8. Send Out Invites (and Track RSVPs!) 
  9. Have a Plan B (and C!) 
  10. Enjoy the Moment! 

1. Define Your Vision: The Core of Your Event 

Before you start planning, take a moment to picture what you want. Are you thinking of a casual backyard BBQ with games, or a classy cocktail party with music, ambient lighting, and hors d’oeuvres? Or perhaps you envision a more intimate gathering where some guests might even be comfortable hosting in their own homes.

Your vision will guide every part of the event, from the venue to the food. It’s about making sure the event reflects your style and the purpose of the celebration. So, take a deep breath and imagine the perfect vibe!


Key Tips: 

  • Stay clear on your vision to make confident decisions. 
  • Think about your guests and what they’ll enjoy. 
  • Match the vibe to the occasion—birthdays are different from corporate events.
  • Consider if some guests might be comfortable hosting in their own homes if that fits your vision. 
  • Your budget will affect how you bring your vision to life.


2. Set Your Budget: The Foundation of Your Event 

Let’s be honest—money matters when planning an event. Start by figuring out how much you can afford to spend. From there, divide it between big costs like the venue and food, and smaller costs like decor and invites. 

And don’t forget to add a little extra for unexpected expenses! 


Key Tips: 

  • Be realistic with your budget from the start. 
  • Research costs by getting quotes from vendors. 
  • Prioritize what matters most to you. 
  • Plan for surprises with a small contingency fund. 

3. Pick the Right Date & Venue: Setting the Scene 

Once you’ve got your vision and budget, it’s time to choose a date and find a venue. Popular dates fill up fast, so start early. Think about what works best for your guests, and choose a venue that fits the event and guest list. 


Key Tips: 

  • Be flexible with dates if needed. 
  • Consider what’s convenient for your guests. 
  • Visit venues in person to see if they fit your vibe. 
  • Don’t forget logistics like parking and accessibility. 

Remember, at Cococabana, we’re here to help you find the perfect venue and negotiate details like setup time so you get the best options! 


4. Make Your Guest List: Who's Coming? 

Now it’s time to decide who you want at your event! Your guest list impacts everything from your budget to the venue size and how much food you’ll need. Start by thinking about who you want to share the day with. Is it just close friends and family, or a bigger group that includes workmates and others? 

Remember, each person adds to the cost, so keep your budget in mind. Also, decide if guests can bring someone or if children are invited, as this affects your final numbers. 

Key Tips: 

  • Start early so you can adjust your plan if needed. 
  • Be clear in your invites if plus ones or children are welcome.
  • Track RSVPs to make sure you have the right numbers for food and seating. 

5. Plan the Menu: What Will They Eat? 

Food is often the highlight of any event, so take your time planning the menu. Consider the type of event and the time of day. A brunch might have waffles and mimosas, while a fancy evening party could have a sit-down meal with appetizers. 

Also, make sure to account for dietary needs like vegetarian or gluten-free options. If possible, try the food in advance to make sure it’s exactly what you want. 

Key Tips: 

  • Offer a variety of dishes to cater to everyone’s preferences. 
  • The presentation of the food is important too—make it look good! 
  • Don’t forget to plan the drinks to match your menu. 

6. Decorate: Set the Mood 

Decorations do more than just look nice—they help create the atmosphere for your event. Think about how you can use colors, textures, and lighting to match your theme. Whether it’s flowers or balloons, the options are endless! 

If you're on a tight budget, DIY decor is a great way to add a personal touch. And good lighting can completely transform a space. 

Key Tips: 

  • Use decor to enhance your event’s theme. 
  • Add personal touches that make the event special. 
  • Lighting can change the whole mood—use it creatively. 

7. Entertainment: Keep Everyone Engaged 

Entertainment is key to keeping your guests happy and energized. Whether you choose a live band, DJ, or fun games, great entertainment makes an event unforgettable. 

Pick activities that match your guests’ preferences and your event style. For example, a dance party might suit younger crowds, while live music might work for a more relaxed gathering. 

Key Tips: 

  • Music and entertainment help set the tone of the event. 
  • Think about what your guests will enjoy. 
  • Mix up the activities to keep things interesting throughout the event.

8. Send Out Invites (and Track RSVPs!) 

Your invitations are the first impression of your event, so make them count! The design and wording should match the theme and get your guests excited. Be sure to include important details like the date, time, location, and any special instructions, such as dress code or parking info. Clear invites mean less confusion for your guests. 

Don't forget to track RSVPs! Whether you use an online tool or a simple spreadsheet, keeping track of who's coming will help you finalize numbers for seating and catering. 

Key Tips: 

  • First impressions matter: Invitations set the tone. 
  • Be clear: Include all necessary info. 
  • Stay organized: Track RSVPs to manage your guest list effectively.

9. Have a Backup Plan 

Even the best plans can hit bumps. Rain, vendor issues, or even a power outage can happen, so always have a backup. For outdoor events, consider renting a tent or having an indoor location as a backup. Keep extra supplies like napkins or a first-aid kit handy. Most importantly, stay calm and flexible – a positive attitude will help you handle anything that comes up. 

Key Tips: 

  • Be prepared: Anticipate challenges and have solutions ready. 
  • Stay calm: Keep a positive attitude if things don’t go as planned. 
  • Be flexible: Be ready to adjust if needed. 

10. Enjoy the Day 

You’ve done all the hard work, now it's time to enjoy the event! Delegate tasks to trusted friends or family members, so you can focus on being in the moment. Take time to enjoy the atmosphere and connect with your guests. Capture the special moments with photos and videos to relive the memories later. 

Key Tips: 

  • Relax: Trust your planning and enjoy the event. 
  • Be present: Engage with your guests and enjoy the experience. 
  • Capture memories: Take photos and videos to remember the day.



Our Event Portfolio

At Cococabana, we enjoy putting together various events with attention to detail and creativity. Here are some great events we’ve had the joy of organizing.

 

Conclusion On Essential Event Planning Tips for a Great Celebration 

Planning a great event doesn’t have to be stressful. With these 10 tips, you're ready to create a celebration that matches your vision and leaves your guests impressed. Cococabana is here to help you from start to finish, handling the details so you can focus on enjoying the moment. Ready to bring your event to life? How to Choose the Right Event Planner

1. Know Your Needs & Vision: Laying the Groundwork 

Before you start looking for an event planner, take a moment to think about your event. What are you trying to achieve? Is it a small wedding, a big corporate event, or a birthday party? 

Understanding the type of event, its size, and your budget will help you narrow down your options. You’ll also want to think about the vibe, is it a casual outdoor event, a fancy black-tie affair, or something totally unique? Clear communication about your vision will help you find the right planner. 


Key Points: 

  • Be clear about your needs and vision, the more specific, the better. 
  • Have a realistic budget to guide your search. 
  • Don't forget the vibe, the style and mood of the event are just as important as the details.

2. Research & Shortlist Potential Planners: Casting a Wide Net 

Now that you know what you want, it’s time to start searching for planners. Ask friends, family, or colleagues for recommendations. Personal referrals are a great starting point. 

You can also check online. Look at local planners’ websites and portfolios to see their style and experience. Don’t forget social media, it’s a good way to see their recent work and client feedback. Industry directories or associations are another resource for finding trusted planners. 


Key Points: 

  • Ask for recommendations from people you trust. 
  • Look online for planners' websites, portfolios, and social media profiles. 
  • Use industry resources like directories to find professionals in your area. 

3. Evaluate Experience & Expertise: Finding the Right Fit 

With a shortlist of planners, it’s time to dig deeper. How long have they been in business? What kinds of events do they specialize in? Do they have experience with events similar to yours? Ask for examples or testimonials from past clients. 

You should also ask if they have any special certifications or awards. While not necessary, these can show that they are serious about their profession. 


Key Points: 

  • Experience matters, seasoned planners know how to handle challenges. 
  • Look for planners who specialize in your type of event. 
  • Don’t be shy, ask questions about their process and how they handle surprises. 

Remember, choosing the right event planner will give you peace of mind. Take your time and find someone who matches your vision and experience level. 


4. Communication is Key: Building a Strong Connection 

Good communication is the foundation of a strong partnership with your event planner. You’ll be sharing your ideas, expectations, and concerns with them, so it’s important they truly listen to you. 

Pay attention to how quickly they respond. Do they answer calls or emails promptly? Do they make you feel comfortable asking questions or raising concerns? A good event planner will listen carefully, offer helpful suggestions, and keep you updated throughout the planning. 


Key Points: 

  • Choose a planner who responds quickly and values your time. 
  • Make sure they understand your needs and vision.
  • Their communication should be clear and professional. 
  • Ask how they prefer to communicate and how often you’ll check in. 

5. Check References & Reviews: Learn from Others 

While a planner’s website can look impressive, hearing from past clients can give you deeper insight. Don’t hesitate to ask for references and talk to them about their experience. 

Online reviews are also helpful, but read them carefully. Look for common themes in both good and bad feedback. Do people often praise their organization or problem-solving skills? Or are there repeated complaints about communication or staying on budget? 

In the end, trust your gut. Do you feel confident and comfortable with this planner?


Key Points: 

  • Ask for references and talk to past clients about their experience. 
  • Read online reviews carefully and look for patterns. 
  • Trust your instincts when choosing a planner. 

6. Understand Their Services & Pricing: No Hidden Surprises 

Event planning services can vary a lot, so it’s important to know exactly what’s included. Ask for a detailed breakdown of what they offer and if there are any extra fees. 

Do they provide full-service planning, or do they offer specific services you can pick and choose from? Make sure you get everything in writing and compare quotes from different planners. Also, ask about their payment schedule and cancellation policy. 


Key Points: 

  • Make sure you understand what’s included in their services. 
  • Get a written contract to protect both you and the planner. 
  • Compare quotes from different planners. 
  • Ask if there are any hidden fees. 

 

Related posts:

Top 7 Event Decor Trends

Event Planning Checklist

 

7. Personality & Chemistry Matters: The Human Connection 

You’ll be working closely with your event planner for weeks or months, so it’s important to find someone whose personality matches yours. 

Do you feel a connection when you talk to them? Are they excited about your event and ideas? A great planner will not only be organized and professional but also passionate about making your event a success.


Key Points: 

  • Trust your gut, if it doesn’t feel right, move on to another planner. 
  • Look for enthusiasm and passion for your event. 
  • Make sure they understand and support your vision. 

8. Availability & Flexibility: Handling the Unexpected 

Before hiring a planner, check if they’re available on your event date. Popular planners often get booked early, especially during busy seasons. 

Also, ask how flexible they are. Sometimes things don’t go as planned, and you need a planner who can handle changes smoothly. A good planner will adapt and find solutions to keep your event on track. 

Lastly, ask if they’ll be present at your event. Having them there can give you peace of mind and ensure everything runs smoothly. 


Key Points: 

  • Book early: Make sure your planner is available for your event date. 
  • Flexibility matters: Choose someone who can handle unexpected changes. ● On-site presence: Having your planner there on the big day is helpful. 

9. Trust Your Gut: The Final Choice 

After doing your research and talking to different planners, trust your instincts. If something feels off, even if you can’t explain it, it’s okay to keep looking. 

This is your event, and you should feel confident and excited about the planner you choose. Don’t settle, keep searching until you find the perfect match. 


Key Points: 

  • Trust your gut: If something doesn’t feel right, move on. 
  • Feel confident: You should be excited and at ease with your choice. 
  • Don’t rush: The right planner is out there, so take your time to find them.

title: Top 7 Event Decor Trends to Transform Your Event Space in 2024
author: Christine Osakwe
description: Here are the Top 7 Event Decor Trends to Transform Your Event Space in 2024: Sustainable & Eco-Friendly Decor, Bold Colors & Patterns, Personalized & Interactive Installations, Tech-Infused Decor, Bringing the Outdoors In, Minimalist & Monochromatic Designs, and Nostalgia-Inspired Decor
html:
Think about walking into an event space that instantly grabs your attention. Every color, texture, and detail comes together to create a beautiful experience. That’s the power of good décor. At Cococabana, we know great décor makes events unforgettable. In 2024, keeping up with the latest trends will help your event space truly shine.


Trend 1: Sustainable & Eco-Friendly Decor 

As people become more aware of the environment, eco-friendly events are not just trendy – they’re a responsibility. Guests today appreciate events that care about the planet, and using eco-friendly décor is a great way to show this. Think about using recycled materials, natural items, and locally grown flowers. Imagine wooden tables decorated with green plants or old glass jars turned into candle holders. Sustainable décor not only helps the environment but also boosts your event’s reputation by showing you're committed to responsible practices. 


Trend 2: Bold Colors & Patterns 

Say goodbye to soft colors and say hello to a burst of bold colors! In 2024, bright and lively color schemes are in. Think of fuchsia pinks, electric blues, and sunny yellows. Don’t hesitate to mix and match them to create a fun and exciting vibe. Patterns are also big, adding extra interest to your event. From geometric designs to floral patterns, you can use them on tablecloths, backdrops, or even the floor. The key is to balance these bold elements with the overall look of your event, making sure everything works together. 


Trend 3: Personalized & Interactive Installations 

Generic décor is a thing of the past. Events now need personal touches that reflect the theme or brand. Custom installations are the way to go, creating stunning pieces that leave guests in awe. Picture a large floral design spelling out your company’s name or a photo booth that takes guests into a different world. These personal elements not only make the event look amazing but also encourage guests to engage and participate. With options like Instagram-ready backdrops and immersive art pieces, you can create an event that's truly unique.


Trend 4: Tech-Infused Decor 

In today's world, technology is a big part of our lives, and it’s also changing event decor. Adding tech elements to your event can make it exciting and unforgettable for your guests. Think of stunning light shows that move with the music, projections that turn walls into beautiful scenes, or interactive displays that let guests join in the fun. These tech additions can make your event stand out. 

But it’s important to choose tech that matches your event’s theme and goals. Don’t use technology just because it’s cool; make sure it fits the mood and purpose of your event. Ideas like LED dance floors, 3D projections, or even virtual reality can take your event to the next level if they align with your vision. 


Trend 5: Bringing the Outdoors In 

With people spending more time in cities, many are craving a connection to nature. Bringing nature indoors, also called biophilic design, can create a relaxing and welcoming atmosphere at your event. Think of green plants, wooden or stone materials, and even water features like fountains or small waterfalls. These natural touches not only look beautiful but can also help guests feel calm and refreshed. 

Imagine a reception area filled with hanging plants, a cozy seating area with wicker furniture, or a dining space lit by natural sunlight. By including these natural elements, you can make your event feel peaceful and connected to the outdoors. 


Trend 6: Minimalist & Monochromatic Designs 

Sometimes, simplicity is key. Minimalist and single-color designs offer a sense of elegance and class. By keeping things simple with clean lines and a limited color scheme, you can create a space that feels polished and stylish. 

Picture a completely white reception hall with simple flower arrangements or a formal event with sleek black and gold decor. The trick to minimalist design is using different materials and textures to add interest. For example, velvet curtains, metallic touches, or textured tablecloths can make the space feel richer. 

Using just one color doesn’t have to be dull. By using different shades of the same color, you can create a layered and interesting look. Add small bursts of contrasting color with lights or flowers to catch the eye.


Trend 7: Nostalgia-Inspired Decor 

Take a trip down memory lane! Nostalgia-themed decor is making a comeback by using vintage or retro styles that remind guests of the past. Adding old-fashioned items like vinyl records, vintage furniture, or classic arcade games can make your event feel cozy and familiar. 

Nostalgic decor brings warmth and shared memories, making your event feel more personal. The key is to pick elements that will resonate with your guests. Whether it’s a disco party from the 70s, an 80s arcade theme, or a 90s grunge revival, these touches can add fun and charm to your event.

Conclusion: Elevate Your Event with Exceptional Decor 

Event decor is more than just decorations, it’s a chance to create a memorable experience for your guests. By using the latest trends and personalizing your decor, you can transform your event space into something truly special.
